evidence.claim: Reuters said parliament chose Shehbaz Sharif after a no-confidence vote in a week-long constitutional confrontation, and that the nuclear-armed country was likely to remain prone to political and economic turbulence.
evidence.title: Pakistan parliament elects Sharif PM as Khan MPs quit en masse
evidence.excerpt: Reuters said parliament chose Shehbaz Sharif after a no-confidence vote in a week-long constitutional confrontation, and that the nuclear-armed country was likely to remain prone to political and economic turbulence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting, but the article is a short political summary rather than a nuclear-policy document.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context for inherited constraints, not proof of nuclear conduct.
contrary_evidence: This is broad political context, not direct evidence of nuclear decision-making.

evidence.claim: The federal government instructed PEMRA to lift the ban on broadcasting Imran Khan's speech, and the information minister said the prime minister had directed PEMRA to implement Article 19 of the constitution.
evidence.title: Federal govt issues instructions to PEMRA for lifting ban on broadcasting Imran's speech
evidence.excerpt: The federal government instructed PEMRA to lift the ban on broadcasting Imran Khan's speech, and the information minister said the prime minister had directed PEMRA to implement Article 19 of the constitution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of an official instruction from the prime minister, with clear date and named implementing agency.
evidence.period_fit: Direct November 2022 action inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Sharif through the minister's statement; this is a concrete pro-opposition speech decision, though it followed earlier restrictions.
contrary_evidence: The action came after earlier broadcast restrictions, so it is partial and late rather than a clean baseline reform.

evidence.claim: Sharif strongly condemned the armed intrusion into anchor Shifa Yousafzai's home, asked the Islamabad IG for a report, and directed that the suspects be found and punished under the law.
evidence.title: شفا یوسفزئی کے گھر مسلح افراد کا دھاوا، وزیر اعظم نے واقعے کی رپورٹ طلب کرلی
evidence.excerpt: Sharif strongly condemned the armed intrusion into anchor Shifa Yousafzai's home, asked the Islamabad IG for a report, and directed that the suspects be found and punished under the law.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-language outlet quoting the prime minister and police response; strong for the immediate response, weaker for any broader systemic conclusion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct PM response to an attack on a journalist; it shows a protective reaction to one incident, not durable system-wide protection.
contrary_evidence: The underlying incident shows journalists still faced severe insecurity.
A response to one attack does not prove sustained protection of the press.

evidence.claim: The Federal Investigation Agency detained eight people after they published criticism of the state on Twitter, and Amnesty said the arrests were part of a repressive crackdown on free expression online.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Immediately release eight people arrested over critical tweets
evidence.excerpt: The Federal Investigation Agency detained eight people after they published criticism of the state on Twitter, and Amnesty said the arrests were part of a repressive crackdown on free expression online.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct advocacy alert with a dated incident and specific state agency; the attribution is clear even if the broader pattern remains advocacy-framed.
evidence.period_fit: Direct April 2022 conduct inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The arrests were carried out by FIA under the federal state; direct Sharif ordering is not established, but the pattern persisted under his government.
contrary_evidence: The source does not prove Sharif personally ordered the arrests.

evidence.claim: Families of the disappeared and activists who protest peacefully are sometimes met with violence by the state, intimidation, and arbitrary detention or arrest for exercising peaceful assembly.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Braving the Storm: Enforced disappearances and the right to protest in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Families of the disappeared and activists who protest peacefully are sometimes met with violence by the state, intimidation, and arbitrary detention or arrest for exercising peaceful assembly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed campaign digest with direct rights-violation findings and date-specific framing; strong on the existence of the abuse pattern.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 reporting on protest and disappearance-related abuse.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is state-level attribution rather than a single Sharif order; it captures the domestic safety climate under his government but much of the problem predates him.
contrary_evidence: Some of the underlying disappearance problem predates Sharif and is not uniquely attributable to him.

evidence.claim: Pakistani police fired teargas, baton-charged, and detained supporters of ousted PM Imran Khan to stop them reaching Islamabad to demand fresh elections.
evidence.title: Pakistan police fire teargas, baton-charge, round up supporters of ousted PM Khan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistani police fired teargas, baton-charged, and detained supporters of ousted PM Imran Khan to stop them reaching Islamabad to demand fresh elections.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with concrete incident details and witnesses; attribution to national-level command is indirect, but the protest suppression itself is well documented.
evidence.period_fit: Direct May 2022 protest suppression inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The action was carried out by police and other authorities during the Sharif era; direct PM ordering is not shown, so attribution is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: Authorities justified the response as keeping order around an unannounced road blockade.
Direct Sharif instruction is not established in the report.

evidence.claim: RSF said it had registered nine cases of intimidation of Pakistani journalists by army-related agencies since Shehbaz Sharif became prime minister and warned the harassment was undermining democracy.
evidence.title: Behind Pakistan’s civilian government, army tightens its grip on journalists
evidence.excerpt: RSF said it had registered nine cases of intimidation of Pakistani journalists by army-related agencies since Shehbaz Sharif became prime minister and warned the harassment was undermining democracy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated advocacy report with named cases and explicit attribution; strong on the pattern, though the military-centric attribution limits direct PM culpability.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022, squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: RSF links the harassment mainly to army-related agencies, which limits direct attribution to Sharif but still places the pattern under his watch.
contrary_evidence: RSF itself says the military was acting behind the scenes, so this is not a clean civilian-only responsibility case.

evidence.claim: ARY News was taken off the air in most major Pakistani cities and its news director was arrested; RSF said the civilian government was responsible for the latest attacks on the media while the military intervened behind the scenes.
evidence.title: Pakistani TV news channel taken off the air, news director arrested
evidence.excerpt: ARY News was taken off the air in most major Pakistani cities and its news director was arrested; RSF said the civilian government was responsible for the latest attacks on the media while the military intervened behind the scenes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific dated incident with direct reporting and explicit attribution commentary, though the source itself notes behind-the-scenes military involvement.
evidence.period_fit: August 2022 action in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The report holds the current civilian government responsible for the latest attack while also pointing to military influence, so attribution is shared and incomplete rather than purely personal to Sharif.
contrary_evidence: The source says the military high command stamped the censorship, limiting direct attribution to the civilian prime minister.
The same report emphasizes recurring pressure across alternating governments.

evidence.claim: HRW said Pakistani authorities harassed and prosecuted human rights defenders and journalists for criticizing government policies, used blasphemy accusations and sedition laws against opponents and journalists, and failed to protect minorities and other at-risk groups in 2022.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Rights Besieged Amid Political Turmoil
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Pakistani authorities harassed and prosecuted human rights defenders and journalists for criticizing government policies, used blasphemy accusations and sedition laws against opponents and journalists, and failed to protect minorities and other at-risk groups in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A retrospective annual report with concrete 2022 incidents and multiple corroborating themes; strong synthesis though it attributes broadly to authorities rather than a single decision-maker.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but directly about 2022 conduct under the Sharif government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is to Pakistani authorities during 2022, including the Sharif government, but the report does not isolate direct prime-ministerial commands.
contrary_evidence: This is a broad retrospective and not proof of a single Sharif order for each incident.
Some abuses predate Sharif and are institutional rather than personal.

unresolved_gaps: No independent 2022 evidence of a Sharif-chaired NCA session or any doctrine, custody, or command-and-control reform.
No direct evidence of Sharif's handling of dual-use, proliferation, cyber, biosecurity, or AI-risk policy in 2022.
The April 2022 Afghanistan strike allegation remains unresolved by an independent finding or clear attribution chain.
No formal ceasefire or settlement output with India or Afghanistan beyond public diplomacy and border-management statements.
Primary court orders or audit findings on the Ramzan Sugar Mills and Ashiana matters are still needed to separate allegations from a durable personal-nexus finding.
The appointment/favoritism question still lacks stronger evidence about whether key personnel choices reflected merit or protection of insiders.
